chapter.heading: Longing for Zion in a Foreign Land
chapter.v:
By the
rivers of Babylon,There we sat down, yea, we weptWhen we remembered Zion. [Is. 56:9-12; Jer.]

We hung
our harpsUpon the willows in the midst of it. [Ex. 32:34]

For there
those who carried us away captive asked of us a song,And those who plundered us requested mirth,Saying, “Sing us one of the songs of Zion!” [Is. 11:11, 12, 16; Jer. 32:37]

How shall
we sing the Lord’s songIn a foreign land? [Jer. 3:15; [Ezek.]

If I
forget you, O Jerusalem,Let my right hand forget its skill! [Is. 4:2; 11:1; 40:10, 11; Jer. 33:14; [Dan. 9:24; Zech. 6:12]; Matt. 1:1, 6 $; Luke 3:31; [John 1:45; 7:42] f Ps. 72:2; Is. 9:7; 32:1, 18; [Dan.]

If I
do not remember you,Let my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth—If I do not exalt JerusalemAbove my chief joy. [Deut. 33:28; Jer. 30:10; Zech. 14:11 h Jer. 32:37] [Is. 45:24; Jer. 33:16; [Dan. 9:24; Rom. 3:22; 1 Cor. 1:30] $]

Remember, O
Lord, against the sons of EdomThe day of Jerusalem,Who said, “Raze it, raze it,To its very foundation!”

O daughter
of Babylon, who are to be destroyed,Happy the one who repays you as you have served us! [Is. 43:5, 6; Ezek. 34:13; Amos 9:14,]

Happy the
one who takes and dashesYour little ones against the rock! [Jer. 8:18; Hab.]
